subject: Architecture
title: Daylighting: Designing with Sunshine
description: Learn Daylighting: Designing with Sunshine in one minute.

hook.text: Artificial lighting uses 20% of all electricity in commercial buildings. Sunlight is free.

buildup.text: Light shelves, clerestory windows, and light tubes bounce daylight deep into building interiors.

discovery.text: Studies show workers in daylit offices are 18% more productive and report better sleep quality.

twist.text: Too much glass causes glare and overheating. Good daylighting balances light with thermal comfort.

climax.text: Dynamic glass can tint automatically, adjusting from clear to dark as the sun moves across the sky.

punchline.text: The best lighting system has been shining for 4.6 billion years.

quiz.question: How much more productive are workers in daylit offices?

details.summary: Daylighting design maximizes natural light penetration to reduce electric lighting needs, which account for 15-25% of a commercial building's energy use. Light shelves, clerestory windows, light tubes, and reflective surfaces can deliver usable daylight up to 12 meters from a window wall.
details.whyItMatters: Daylight improves productivity, health, sleep cycles, and mood while reducing energy costs. Buildings designed for daylighting use less electricity and create better spaces for occupants — making it architecture's rare win-win-win solution.
takeaways: Natural light reduces electric lighting energy by 15-25%
Light shelves and tubes deliver daylight up to 12 meters deep
Daylight improves occupant health, productivity, and mood

faq.question: What is a light shelf?
faq.answer: A horizontal surface mounted at window height that bounces sunlight up onto the ceiling, reflecting it deeper into the room. The top surface is reflective, while a shade below prevents direct glare. Light shelves can push effective daylight penetration from 4 meters to 12 meters from the window.

faq.question: Can you have too much daylight?
faq.answer: Yes — uncontrolled direct sunlight causes glare, overheating, and UV damage to interiors. Good daylighting design diffuses and redirects light rather than simply admitting it. External shading, internal blinds, and light-redirecting glazing control intensity while maximizing useful illumination.
